statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail 5 (low) through every scheduled CME weekend halt hour and 12 to 13 (low) in the four reopen hours; Stress 25 (moderate) now, rising to 47 (elevated) at the reopen; Confidence 60 (solid).
recommendation: Descriptive only. CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in the first twenty hours covered here and Tail stays far below the block threshold for both NQ_FUTURES and NAS100_CFD. Stress runs from 25 to 47 as unpriced weekend information accumulates ahead of the reopen and the 1 to 4 September data stack, and Confidence eases from 60 to 47 as the Friday reference tape ages before recovering into the reopen when live price discovery would resume. No danger window is published, because no observed one-way structure exists and none can form while the venue is closed.
headline: Weekend halt, hour 30: NDX 29,433.43 (-0.70%) closed near the low of a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range, NQ 29,491.75, VIX 14.43, and a post-Jackson-Hole repricing that lifted September hike odds to about 57%; Globex reopens Sunday 22:00 UTC as the twenty-first slot of this window
body: CME Globex has been halted since Friday 21:00 UTC and is scheduled to reopen at Sunday 30 August 22:00 UTC, which falls inside this window as its final four slots, so the first twenty hours assessed here are a closed venue with no Nasdaq-100 price discovery; NQ last traded at 20:59 UTC on 28 August. The reference tape was re-verified against primary sources this run and was unchanged: cash NDX closed 29,433.43, down 0.70 percent or 208.13 points, inside a 29,383.92 to 29,752.78 range against a 29,641.56 previous close, finishing near the lower end of that range; NQ futures last printed 29,491.75, down 0.69 percent or 204.00 points, in a 29,436.75 to 29,811.50 range; VIX finished at 14.43, down 0.55 percent, within a 14.13 to 14.84 range against a 14.51 previous close. The Federal Reserve H.15 daily release still carries 27 August as its most recent column, at 4.20 percent for the 2-year and 4.67 percent for the 10-year, because the 28 August column has not yet been published; verified reporting refined this run places the Friday 2-year at about 4.35 percent, some 12 basis points higher on the day, and the 10-year at about 4.72 percent, after Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's Jackson Hole remarks that inflation is running too high, which markets read as leaning toward a September increase and which lifted odds of a 25 basis point hike to about 57 percent from roughly 35 percent the prior day. That repricing remains the single most important item in the current evidence set, and the shape of it is materially Tail-limiting: the front end moved roughly three times as far as the long end, which is the signature of a rotation in the expected policy path rather than of the broad discount-rate repricing that denies mean reversion. The rest of the cross-asset picture is coherent with that reading: gold fell 2.88 percent, the semiconductor complex led the drag with the Semiconductors group down about 2.9 percent and Semiconductor Equipment down about 4.0 percent and Technology down about 1.4 percent, yet the Dow finished effectively flat at minus 0.02 percent, Communication Services gained about 1.4 percent and Consumer Cyclical about 1.4 percent, five of the eight tracked megacaps still closed higher, and VIX declined on the day rather than bidding. WTI settled at 83.44 dollars, down 0.11 percent on the day and about 4 percent lower on the week, re-verified against a primary commodity source this run, while Strait of Hormuz traffic remains far below pre-conflict levels. That confrontation is a six-month-old condition rather than a new discontinuity, and falling crude into it argues against an energy-driven equity shock, so it is scored as background rather than as a Tail amplifier. Shared delayed cross-asset context was 45 minutes old at assessment time and therefore fresh under the freshness rule; it was used only as confirmation of the verified Friday levels, with all ten requested futures symbols and complete breadth, megacap and semiconductor coverage present and no collector warnings, and it was never used as live price-path evidence. Tail is therefore published at 5 for every scheduled halt hour, because the persistent no-retracement price path that Tail is defined against cannot form in a market that is not open, and at 13, 13, 12 and 12 for the four scheduled reopen hours, where a weekend gap into thin Sunday-evening liquidity is a genuine but conditional possibility that stays far below the 25 block threshold. Stress rises from 25 to 47 across the window because unpriced weekend information accumulates against a dense 1 to 4 September macro stack that runs from ISM Manufacturing and JOLTS on Tuesday through ADP, the Fed Beige Book and the Broadcom results on Wednesday to ISM Services on Thursday and the August payrolls report on Friday. Under the fixed mapping those releases are checkpoints rather than automatic Tail blocks, and no danger window is published because no one-way structure has been observed and none can be observed while the venue is closed.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours run from 02:00 UTC on Saturday 29 August to 01:00 UTC on Sunday 30 August, hours 6 to 29 of the CME weekend halt. The mode was normal in every slot and the mapped policy state never left EA_ON. Tail held the 5 floor in all twenty-four hours, because no venue was open to produce the price-path evidence Tail is defined against. Stress dipped to a 22 trough in the early hours and then rebuilt to a 25 plateau held for the final twenty slots, while Confidence declined steadily from 82 to 60 as the Friday reference tape aged without any new observation to refresh it. No slot was unavailable and no assessment in the window was revised with later information.
outlookSummary: The first twenty hours of this window fall inside the CME weekend halt, so no Nasdaq-100 price path can form in them; Tail is held at 5 throughout, keeping the mapped policy state at EA_ON, and the dominant mode is normal in those slots because a closed market has no structure to classify rather than because conditions are assessed as calm. Stress climbs from 25 to 43 across those hours as unpriced weekend information accumulates against Friday's hawkish front-end repricing and the dense 1 to 4 September macro week, while Confidence decays from 60 to 47 purely through the ageing of the reference tape. The final four slots are the scheduled Globex reopen at 22:00 UTC, the first full hour after it, the hour around the Tokyo cash open and the established Asian session, the first hours in this window that can host observable structure: they are published with conditional Tail readings of 13, 13, 12 and 12 and a mixed mode, which allows for a weekend gap into thin Sunday-evening liquidity while remaining far below the 25 block threshold, and with Confidence recovering from 55 to 61 as live price discovery would resume. Whether the reopen matters for Tail will depend on whether early retracements hold rather than on the size of any gap, and no such structure is observed at publication time.
